reporting-org.narrative: Hague Institute for the Innovation of Law

description.narrative: The overall impact of the programme is to empower people and institutions in the targeted countries to prevent or resolve pressing justice problems. This programme is focussed on a selection of seven countries fall under the priority countries for your ministry: Mali, Nigeria, Burkina Faso, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya and Tunisia.

The programme try to achieve the following five outcomes:Outcome I - Enhanced access to and use by justice sector stakeholders of data and knowledge about justice needs and outcomes of justice journeysOutcome II - Improved capacity of justice practitioners and providers of justice services to resolve the most pressing justice problemsOutcome III - Increased access to and use of justice services for peopleOutcome IV - Strengthened dialogue between justice stakeholders on justice needs to create the necessary political space and an enabling environment for justice innovation and gamechangersOutcome V - Reinforced international, regional, and national networks of people-centred justice

description.narrative: HiiL indicator: # of people whose justice issues can be prevented or resolved by supported startups (m/f)

comment.narrative: MoV: start-up self-reporting and due diligence. Data collection method: Justice Accelerator impact sruvey sent to supported start-ups.

HiiL contributed to access to justice for 142,890 people with approximately 54% beneficiaries being women. This indicator is linked to our Justice Accelerator programme. Based on the self-reported impact numbers from JA startups, we calculate our contribution to this result as: the number of justice problems resolved (not including prevention), adjusted pro-rata (proportionate), and from startups receiving financial or technical assistance in 2024 (time bound).

description.narrative: HiiL indicator: # of justice institutions/organizations adopt guideline based on the co-created implementation plan (also indicate # of justice practitioners working in the concerned field in these institutions/organizations)

comment.narrative: HiiL indicator: # of justice institutions / organisations adopt guideline based on the co-created implementation plan (also indicate # of justice practitioners working in the concerned field in these institutions / organisations)

In the reporting period, we developed and published the 'Ethiopian Land Justice Guidelines: Recommendations and best practices for land dispute resolution.' This brings the total number of guidelines developed since 2021 to four. To date, 1,248 individuals from 32 institutions (26 formal, including the Tunisian Bar Association and the Nigerian Ministry of Justice, and 6 informal, such as the Child Protection Network in Nigeria) have been trained on these guidelines. Measuring guideline adoption is essential for evaluating effectiveness. To allow for adequate implementation, institutional change, and practitioner feedback, adoption measurement activities are scheduled for 2025.
